newsitem.title: INDIA: Slowdown for India firms in first half - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Slowdown for India firms in first half - Reuter poll.

text.p: First half profits of top Indian firms which make up the benchmark Bombay stocks index will see a sharp slowdown, but strong results from banking and auto firms are likely to soften the blow, a Reuters poll found on Tuesday.
The poll of 14 leading securities houses projected an average 20.6 percent rise in the net profit of 30 index firms during the first half ended September 30, 1996 from around 40 percent a year ago.
Net sales growth was pegged at a modest 16.5 percent.

"There's a definite slowdown in growth mainly because the cost of borrowing has gone up and most companies are depositing this money into long-term assets," said Sanjay D'Souza, head of research at Nucleus Securities.
Prime lending rates jumped to 16.5 percent in mid-1996 from 15 a year ago with many companies borrowing at upto 20 percent.
Bank lending rates are currently at 15.5 percent.
"Interest rates were quite high and those companies that didn't have extra money from issuing overseas equity have been hit," said Devesh Kumar, strategist at W.I. Carr.
Analysts said declining global prices of commodities like petrochemicals, aluminium and steel coupled with cuts in import duties of these products would hit several index firms.
"Many index heavyweights are in the commodity business where enough capacity has already come up and they are not even able to increase prices," Kumar said.
Analysts said a new 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax (MAT) on book profits of companies which previously did not pay taxes was also responsible for the slowdown in profit growth.
"MAT is one major factor contributing to the slowdown," said Sanjeev Mohta, head of research at broking firm James Capel B&K.
Analysts slashed earnings forecasts for several index heavyweights including top two private firms Reliance Industries and TISCO after India introduced MAT.
"Falling commodity prices and a cut in import duties have also hit profits," Mohta said.
The poll forecast a 25.8 percent drop in the first half net profit for Reliance -- chiefly due to a provision for MAT and a sharp decline in polyester prices.
The net profit of steel maker TISCO was projected to rise by 12 percent against a whopping 132 percent a year ago. Steel firms TISCO and SAIL have been hit by falling prices and MAT.

India's largest commercial bank State Bank of India (SBI) emerged the star performer in the Reuters poll. Analysts said reduced provisions would provide a major boost to SBI's bottomline and forecast a steep 177.7 percent jump in first half net profit to an average 6.4 billion rupees.
Auto firms TELCO, Bajaj Auto, Mahindra & Mahindra were outperformers with analysts projecting an average 41 percent growth in their net profits, chiefly driven by higher volumes.
